blocks.content: Sockets are the mechanism that finally delivers on a promise made back in the message passing chapter: a communication model that works identically whether the two communicating processes sit on the same machine or on entirely separate machines connected only by a network. Every pipe, shared memory segment, and message queue covered so far in this course has been strictly limited to processes on one single machine.

This chapter closes out the practical IPC mechanisms covered in this module by showing how sockets extend the same send and receive spirit from the message passing chapter into a genuinely general purpose, network capable communication endpoint.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507613-227386864.png
1. What a Socket Actually Is

A socket is a communication endpoint, an abstraction the operating system provides that a process can send data to and receive data from, without needing to know or care whether the process on the other end is running locally or across a network entirely. This uniformity is the single most important idea in this chapter.

Underneath, a socket is represented, exactly like an open file, as a file descriptor, tying directly back to the file operations chapter. This is a deliberate design choice: once a socket connection is established, the exact same read, write, and close system calls used on ordinary files work on it too, no separate, socket specific data transfer API is required.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507613-80270813.png
2. Unix Domain Sockets vs Internet Sockets
blocks.text: 2. Unix Domain Sockets vs Internet Sockets

blocks.content: Two broad families of sockets exist, distinguished by how an endpoint is addressed. A Unix domain socket is identified by a path on the local file system, exactly like a named pipe from the pipes chapter, and can only ever be used for communication between processes on the same machine.

An internet socket is instead identified by an IP address and a port number, and works across an actual network connecting genuinely separate machines, or equally well between two processes on the very same machine addressing each other through the local loopback address.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507614-786484826.png
blocks.alt: Unix Domain Sockets vs Internet Sockets

3. TCP vs UDP: Two Very Different Reliability Guarantees
blocks.text: 3. TCP vs UDP: Two Very Different Reliability Guarantees

blocks.content: Internet sockets come in two fundamentally different flavors, matching two different underlying network protocols. A TCP, stream, socket is connection oriented: it establishes an explicit connection first, and then guarantees data arrives reliably and in the exact order it was sent, retransmitting anything lost along the way.

A UDP, datagram, socket makes no such guarantee at all. It is connectionless, sends individual, independent packets with no ordering or delivery guarantee whatsoever, and in exchange carries meaningfully lower overhead, no connection setup, no retransmission bookkeeping, making it the right choice for workloads that value low latency over perfect reliability, like real time video or certain gaming traffic.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507614-130715607.png
blocks.alt: TCP vs UDP: Two Very Different Reliability Guarantees

blocks.content: {"headers":["Property","TCP, stream socket","UDP, datagram socket"],"rows":[["Connection required first","Yes","No"],["Delivery guaranteed","Yes, retransmits lost data","No"],["Ordering guaranteed","Yes","No"],["Relative overhead","Higher","Lower"]]}
4. The Server Side Sequence

Setting up a server socket follows a well defined, standard sequence of calls. socket creates a new communication endpoint. bind attaches that endpoint to a specific local address and port, claiming it for this server. listen marks the socket as ready to accept incoming connection requests. accept then blocks until a client actually connects, and returns a brand new, separate connected socket specifically for that one client, letting the original listening socket keep waiting for further new connections.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507614-492931555.png
5. The Client Side Sequence

A client follows a much shorter sequence. socket creates its own endpoint, exactly like on the server side, and connect requests an actual connection to a specific server address and port. Once connect succeeds, the client can read and write on that socket exactly like the server does on its own accepted connection.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507614-456245681.png
6. The Handshake: Server and Client Together
blocks.text: 6. The Handshake: Server and Client Together

blocks.content: Putting both sides together completes the picture. A client sends a connection request toward a server address it already knows. The server, already listening, has its accept call return with a brand new connected socket specifically dedicated to that one client. From that point forward, both sides simply read and write on their respective connected sockets, exactly like ordinary file descriptors.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507940-348695436.png
blocks.alt: The Handshake: Server and Client Together

blocks.content: 7. Why Sockets Generalize Where Other IPC Mechanisms Cannot
blocks.text: 7. Why Sockets Generalize Where Other IPC Mechanisms Cannot

blocks.content: Every other IPC mechanism covered across this module, pipes, shared memory, message queues, is fundamentally restricted to processes running on the same physical machine. Sockets specifically do not carry this restriction, the exact same API, socket, connect or bind and listen, read, write, close, works completely identically whether the other endpoint is a process on the same machine or halfway around the world across a real network.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785409507940-93877817.png
blocks.alt: Why Sockets Generalize Where Other IPC Mechanisms Cannot

blocks.title: Tying directly back to the message passing chapter
blocks.content: This is exactly the property the message passing chapter identified as message passing central advantage over shared memory: no requirement for directly shared physical memory means the same model extends naturally across a network. Sockets are the concrete, real world mechanism that actually delivers on that promise.
8. Common Mistakes and Interview Angle

["Assuming a socket needs an entirely separate API from ordinary file operations, when a connected socket is itself just a file descriptor, and read, write, and close all work on it exactly as they do on any open file.","Assuming TCP is always the right choice simply because it is more reliable, when UDP lower overhead is a genuine, deliberate tradeoff appropriate for latency sensitive workloads that can tolerate occasional loss.","Forgetting that a Unix domain socket, despite using the same general socket API, is still restricted to local, same machine communication, exactly like a named pipe."]
items: Assuming a socket needs an entirely separate API from ordinary file operations, when a connected socket is itself just a file descriptor, and read, write, and close all work on it exactly as they do on any open file.

Assuming TCP is always the right choice simply because it is more reliable, when UDP lower overhead is a genuine, deliberate tradeoff appropriate for latency sensitive workloads that can tolerate occasional loss.
Forgetting that a Unix domain socket, despite using the same general socket API, is still restricted to local, same machine communication, exactly like a named pipe.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.content: Be ready to walk through the standard server sequence, socket, bind, listen, accept, and the client sequence, socket, connect, from memory, and to explain the TCP versus UDP tradeoff precisely in terms of reliability versus overhead, not just as a vague distinction.

This closes the concrete IPC mechanisms covered in this module. The remaining chapters revisit pipes and signals specifically through the lens of this module IPC framework, tying every mechanism in this course together into one coherent picture.
